October 28, 2026
Canine Osteosarcoma: Amputation, Chemotherapy, Costs, and Clinical Trials in 2026
Osteosarcoma is the most common bone cancer in dogs, and it hides a hard truth: even when the visible tumor is removed, microscopic cancer has almost always already spread. This guide explains what that means for treatment, what standard care costs, the survival numbers families deserve to know, and the trials working to break the ceiling in 2026.
By
Brycen Levings
Read More
September 21, 2026
Anal Sac Adenocarcinoma (AGASACA) in Dogs: Treatment, Costs, and Clinical Trials in 2026
Apocrine gland anal sac adenocarcinoma is an aggressive tumor that often spreads to lymph nodes early and can send calcium levels dangerously high. But with surgery and modern multimodal care, many dogs live well beyond two years. This guide explains the disease, its costs, and the clinical trials expanding options in 2026.
By
Brycen Levings
Read More
August 26, 2026
Canine Histiocytic Sarcoma: Breeds at Risk, Treatment, Costs, and Clinical Trials in 2026
Histiocytic sarcoma is an aggressive cancer of the immune system with a strong breed signature — Bernese Mountain Dogs, Flat-Coated Retrievers, Rottweilers, and Golden Retrievers are especially at risk. This guide explains the localized and disseminated forms, what treatment costs, and the clinical trials expanding options in 2026.
